newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kim rallies nation to revive economy.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kim rallies nation to revive economy.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Saturday urged his nation to join the government's campaign to revive the ailing economy by strengthening corporate competitiveness.

"I earnestly call upon all industrial workers to join actively in the national movement to strengthen competitiveness by 10 percent or more," Kim told a ceremony held in Seoul to mark the 33rd Trade Day.
Kim also repeated his assertion that next year's current account deficit could be halved if the country pooled its efforts.
"If and when we pool all our efforts in productive endeavours, I believe next year the current account deficit will be reduced by half or more from this year's level," Kim said.
The central Bank of Korea on Friday said this year's current account deficit was expected to balloon to about $22 billion from last year's $8.95 billion.
The bank also forecast the real gross domestic product (GDP) growth would slow to 6.9 percent this year from a 9.0 percent rise in 1995.
The South Korean economy ran into trouble early this year after plunging international prices began to hit the nation's major exports, especially semiconductors.

Memory chip producers, which accounted for nearly 20 percent of South Korea's total exports last year, were badly hit as prices for 16 megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips fell 70 to 80 percent from a year ago.
